conditions.note: the agent backend CAN run a model on this same card, but whether one was resident during a given run is not assumed either way: every run record stores the free VRAM reported by /system_stats immediately before that run, and `run_workflow.py --cold` can clear the card first to make the starting state defined. Measured on 04.11 the five headless runs began with 10980, 4531, 1389, 841 and 165 MiB free — the largest peak (10742 MiB) happened when the card was empty, so an earlier blanket claim that a chat model was sitting on the GPU during these rows is not true of them and was removed
conditions.seed_note: fixed in all three graphs (the krea2 KSampler widget, the LCSeed node feeding the MOSS sampler, the Seed node of the Qwen graph); a stale seed number still stored in the MOSS sampler widget is overridden by its link
conditions.canvas_note: NOT unified today, and this is a real difference in cost. Measured from the saved result images on 03.11 (not from the graphs' widgets): the MOSS graph generated 1024x576 (its aspect node shows custom 1024x1024, but an incoming link overrides that widget — a stored value is not what ran; the 2052x576 file in the same folder is the source+result stitch, not a canvas), the Qwen graph generated 1049x590 (a ~0.59 megapixel crop chosen around the touched mask). The Krea2 graph resizes to 1024x576 before the latent. All three are now close to 1024x576, so the cost comparison is roughly fair — the remaining difference is the Qwen crop. Each row states the real size of the saved result image

runs.pair_note: result image matched by save time and aspect, not by counter: the result node is a separate SaveImage node with its own counter (this run: result counter 00113, depth pair 00004). Chose 1024x576 (last image saved at or before its own depth map, same aspect as it); not chosen: krea2_edit_00112_.png 1024x576 at 00:28:18 — the canvas column is indicative until the graph's result SaveImage node uses the graph id and the measurement nodes share its counter; the two maps of this pair were written 54 s apart: the counter matched them, but a run that reused a cached source map writes only its own depth_out, so this pair spans two executions. The depth numbers stay comparable (the source map of a fixed input photo is bit-identical run to run, verified on all three graphs), but this row cannot carry one run's time or memory
runs.verdict: global geometry held + no measurable depth change (0.31 % of the pixels off, under half the 1 % camera-nudge floor of 1.47 %)
